questions.q: A deployed churn model's endpoint still returns 200 OK, but average customer spend in production is now much higher than in the training data. What is this called?
options: Data drift
A deployment failure
Prediction drift
Overfitting
questions.explain: Data drift is a change in the distribution of the model's inputs compared with the reference (usually training) data. Prediction drift is a change in the outputs.

questions.q: In Azure ML model monitoring, what makes an alert fire?
options: Any change at all in the data
A metric or test statistic exceeding a threshold you configured
The endpoint returning an HTTP error
The model being older than 30 days
questions.explain: Azure ML compares production distributions with the baseline and notifies you when a score exceeds a user-specified threshold, by email or through Event Grid.

questions.q: Why are drift signals often more useful than model performance signals for an early warning?
options: Drift signals are always more accurate than accuracy
Performance can never be measured in Azure ML
Drift signals only work on images
Performance signals need ground truth labels, which often arrive late, while drift can be measured as soon as data arrives
questions.explain: You only know who actually churned weeks later, but you can compare input distributions the day the data arrives.

questions.q: In the local experiment, the drifted week had PSI of about 0.57 and the normal week about 0.01. What does that tell you?
options: The two weeks are equally similar to training data
The normal week has drifted more
The drifted week's distribution differs strongly from the reference
PSI cannot distinguish the weeks
questions.explain: A PSI near zero means the distributions match; a large value means they differ substantially. Thresholds such as 0.1 and 0.25 are common rules of thumb, not Azure settings.

questions.q: You deploy a model to a batch endpoint and want Azure ML to monitor it. What does the documentation say about production data?
options: Azure ML collects it automatically for batch endpoints
Monitoring is not possible for batch endpoints
You are responsible for collecting the production inference data yourself
Only the model file is needed
questions.explain: Automatic data collection covers online endpoints. For batch endpoints or models deployed elsewhere, you collect the data and point the monitor at it.
